plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped lavender-pink flowers rise straight out of bare ground, with no leaves in sight. The foliage appeared months earlier and has already died back. Whole meadows can look as if they were scattered with pale crocuses overnight.
plants.location: Meadows and gardens across Europe, in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Despite the name, it is not a true crocus and has no connection to saffron. All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a powerful toxin. Plant breeders also use colchicine to double the chromosome count of other plants.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems carry dense clusters of daisy-like flowers with purple or pink rays around golden centers. They glow in prairies, damp meadows and roadsides just as other flowers fade. Migrating butterflies and late-season bees rely on them.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through autumn (August to late October)
plants.location: Meadows and wet ground in eastern and central North America, in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: New England asters are an important late-season nectar source for migrating monarch butterflies, which refuel on them during their long journey south.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: South Africa's national flower has a dinner-plate-sized bloom. Rows of pink-tipped, silky bracts surround a central cone, so it looks like a crown. It grows on rocky mountain slopes in the fynbos.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (roughly July–October)
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa, in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The genus is named after Proteus, the shape-shifting Greek sea god. The name refers to how much the many protea species vary in form.
